level.title: Elementary: city, travel, routines, health
goals: Find your way around a city
Describe routines and make future plans

lessons.title: Around the city (ESTAR)
lessons.learn: SER is for WHO you are; ESTAR is for WHERE you are. ESTOY = I am (located), ESTÁS = you are, ESTÁ = it is. La estación ESTÁ allí = The station is over there. Add IZQUIERDA (left) and DERECHA (right) and you can follow any directions.

grammar.title: ESTAR for location: estoy, estás, está
grammar.explain: ESTAR answers WHERE. ESTOY EN CASA = I am at home. Never use SER for location! Also learn CERCA (near) and LEJOS (far): Está cerca = It is near.
mistakes: Saying SOY en casa — location is always ESTAR.
Saying ESTÁ for yourself — I am = ESTOY.

dialogue.en: Excuse me, where is the station?
It is over there, on the right.
Is it far?
No, it is near. Five minutes.

lessons.title: Travel and the past
lessons.learn: Talk about finished trips with the PRETÉRITO (simple past). For -AR verbs: HABLÉ (I spoke), HABLASTE (you spoke), HABLÓ (he/she spoke). VIAJÉ A ESPAÑA = I travelled to Spain. One accent mark changes everything!

grammar.title: Past -AR: hablé, hablaste, habló
grammar.explain: Take off -AR, add -É (I), -ASTE (you), -Ó (he/she). Viajé = I travelled. These are finished, done actions: AYER (yesterday) loves the pretérito.
mistakes: Saying HABLO for the past — past I = HABLÉ (with accent!).
Forgetting AYER goes with finished past, not present.

lessons.title: En el tren: billetes, andenes, retrasos
lessons.learn: Station Spanish is compact: UN BILLETE PARA SEVILLA, POR FAVOR · ¿DE QUÉ ANDÉN SALE? · LLEVO VEINTE MINUTOS DE RETRASO. «para» marks the destination of a ticket.

grammar.title: Tickets and connections
grammar.pattern: un billete para + city · ¿de qué andén sale? · hay que hacer transbordo
grammar.explain: Un billete de ida y vuelta para Sevilla, por favor. ¿Hay que hacer transbordo en Córdoba? «para» marks the destination; «a» marks the movement of the train.

examples.en: I want a ticket to Seville.

examples.r: deh keh ahn-DEN SAH-leh el tren?
examples.en: Which platform does the train leave from?

examples.t: El tren lleva veinte minutos de retraso.
examples.r: el tren YEH-vah BAYN-teh mee-NOO-tohs deh reh-TRAH-soh.
examples.en: The train is twenty minutes late.

mistakes.wrong: El tren sale de andén cinco.
mistakes.right: El tren sale del andén cinco.

dialogue.t: Un billete para Sevilla, por favor.
dialogue.r: oon bee-YEH-teh PAH-rah seh-BEE-yah, por fah-BOR.
dialogue.en: A ticket to Seville, please.
Single or return?

dialogue.t: Ida y vuelta. ¿Hay que hacer transbordo?
dialogue.r: EE-dah ee BWEHL-tah. eye keh ah-SEHR trahns-BOR-doh?
dialogue.en: Return. Do I have to change?

dialogue.t: No, directo. Sale del andén siete en diez minutos.
dialogue.r: noh, dee-REK-toh. SAH-leh del ahn-DEN SYEH-teh en DYEHZ mee-NOO-tohs.
dialogue.en: No, direct. It leaves from platform seven in ten minutes.

lessons.title: Daily routines (reflexive verbs)
lessons.learn: Routines use REFLEXIVE verbs: the action goes back to you. ME LEVANTO = I get (myself) up. ME = myself, TE = yourself, SE = himself/herself. Every morning runs on ME/TE/SE!

grammar.title: Reflexive ME/TE/SE: me levanto
grammar.explain: LEVANTARSE = to get up. ME LEVANTO (I get up), TE LEVANTAS (you get up), SE LEVANTA (he/she gets up). The little word before the verb points back at the person.

examples.en: Do you shower in the morning?

mistakes: Saying LEVANTO without ME — it means 'I lift', not 'I get up'!
Mixing TE and SE: TE = you, SE = he/she.

dialogue.en: What time do you get up?

dialogue.t: Me levanto a las siete y me ducho.
dialogue.r: meh leh-VAHN-toh ah lahs SYEH-teh ee meh DOO-choh.
dialogue.en: I get up at seven and shower.
And do you eat breakfast?
Yes, I have breakfast with my family.

lessons.title: Health and future plans
lessons.learn: At the doctor: ME DUELE LA CABEZA = my head hurts (to me it pains the head). For plans, Spanish loves IR A + verb: VOY A VIAJAR = I am going to travel. Easy future, no new endings!

grammar.title: Future with IR A: voy a viajar
grammar.explain: VOY = I go, VAS = you go, VA = he/she goes. VOY A + verb = I am going to…: VOY A COMER = I am going to eat. The second verb never changes!
mistakes: Changing the second verb: VOY A VIAJAR, never VOY A VIAJO.
Forgetting A: VOY A comer, not VOY comer.

dialogue.en: Doctor, my head hurts.
Do you have a fever?
No, but I am going to rest.
Good. You are going to be fine.

lessons.title: En el médico: síntomas y consejos
lessons.learn: Illness is said with tener and doler: TENGO DOLOR DE CABEZA · ME DUELE LA GARGANTA. The doctor answers with debería: DEBERÍA DESCANSAR — advice, not an order.

grammar.title: Symptoms and advice
grammar.pattern: tengo dolor de … · me duele / me duelen … · debería + infinitive
grammar.explain: Me duele la cabeza y tengo fiebre. El médico dice: «Debería descansar y beber agua.» doler agrees with the thing that hurts: me duele la cabeza, me duelen los pies.

examples.en: You should rest for two days.

mistakes.why: The pain's location takes bare de: dolor de garganta.
doler takes the person as indirect object: me duele.

dialogue.t: Buenos días, tengo cita con la doctora.
dialogue.r: BWEH-nohs DEE-ahs, TEN-goh SEE-tah kohn lah dok-TOH-rah.
dialogue.en: Good morning, I have an appointment with the doctor.
What is wrong with you?

dialogue.t: Me duele la garganta y tengo fiebre.
dialogue.r: meh DWEH-leh lah gar-GAHN-tah ee TEN-goh FYEH-breh.
dialogue.en: My throat hurts and I have a fever.

dialogue.t: Debería descansar y beber mucha agua. Le doy una receta.
dialogue.r: deh-beh-REE-ah des-kahn-SAR ee beh-BEHR MOO-chah AH-gwah. leh doy OO-nah reh-SEH-tah.
dialogue.en: You should rest and drink a lot of water. I'll give you a prescription.

lessons.learn: Shop in Spanish! LA CAMISA (shirt), LOS ZAPATOS (shoes). Point with ESTE (this, near me) and ESE (that, near you): ESTA CAMISA (this shirt), ESE VESTIDO (that dress).

grammar.title: ESTE vs ESE: this vs that
grammar.explain: ESTE/ESTA = this (near me). ESE/ESA = that (near you). They match gender: ESTE libro, ESTA camisa, ESE vestido, ESA tienda.
grammar.pattern: este/esta + near thing · ese/esa + farther thing
mistakes: Saying ESTE camisa — camisa is feminine: ESTA camisa.
Using ESE for things in your hand — near you is ESTE.

lessons.title: Weather and -ER/-IR past
lessons.learn: Weather uses HACER (to make): HACE SOL (it is sunny), HACE FRÍO (it is cold). Past of -ER/-IR verbs: COMÍ (I ate), VIVÍ (I lived), COMISTE, COMIÓ. Same endings for -ER and -IR!

grammar.title: Past -ER/-IR: comí, comiste, comió
grammar.explain: Drop -ER/-IR, add -Í (I), -ISTE (you), -IÓ (he/she). COMER → comí, comiste, comió. VIVIR → viví, viviste, vivió. Accents matter: COMIO (wrong) vs COMIÓ (he ate)!
mistakes: Forgetting the accent: COMIÓ, not COMIO.
Mixing -AR endings: COMÍ (not COMÉ) — -ER past I is -Í.

lessons.title: Cambiar y comparar: demasiado grande, más barato
lessons.learn: Shopping problems need the comparative (MÁS BARATO, MÁS GRANDE, MEJOR) and CAMBIAR. The shop answers with a condition: SI TIENE EL TICKET, LO CAMBIAMOS.

grammar.title: Comparing and exchanging
grammar.pattern: más / menos + adjective + que · demasiado + adjective · ¿puedo cambiarlo?
grammar.explain: Esta camisa es más barata que la otra, pero es demasiado pequeña. ¿Puedo cambiarla? The comparative uses más … que; «tan … como» states equality.

items.q: Say: I am going to study

culture.text: Spanish eating has a rhythm of its own: the mid-morning almuerzo, the late comida around two, and the sobremesa — the time after eating when nobody moves and the talk continues. Tapas are not a starter but a way of eating: small plates shared, ordered in rounds. A2 covers ordering because the phrases are short and real, and the cultural note is that «quedarse de sobremesa» is a compliment to the table, never a delay.

reading.text: A las dos comemos. En la mesa hay pan, tortilla y ensalada. Mi madre pregunta: «¿Quieres más?» Yo digo: «No, gracias, estoy lleno.» Luego nos quedamos de sobremesa: café, charla y ninguna prisa. Por la noche vamos de tapas: dos raciones, una caña y la cuenta, que son nueve euros.
reading.gloss: At two o'clock we eat. On the table there is bread, tortilla and salad. My mother asks: 'Do you want more?' I say: 'No thanks, I'm full.' Then we stay over the sobremesa: coffee, talk and no hurry. At night we go for tapas: two portions, a small beer and the bill, which is nine euros.

listening.script:
Ben: ¿Qué quieres tomar?
Ana: Una caña, por favor.
Ben: ¿Y para comer?
Ana: Una ración de tortilla. Y la cuenta, cuando puedas.
listening.gloss: Ben: What would you like to drink? Ana: A small beer, please. Ben: And to eat? Ana: A portion of tortilla. And the bill, when you can.

idioms.literal: it is to lick one's fingers

mistakes.wrong: Quiero un café, por favor. (to a waiter, first contact)
mistakes.why: Quisiera is the polite request; quiero sounds blunt to a stranger.
Hunger is had: tener, not ser.

mistakes.wrong: La cuenta, cuando puedes. (to a waiter)
mistakes.why: The polite frame takes usted: cuando pueda.

task.title: Order at a bar
task.instructions: Write an eight-line bar dialogue in Spanish: greet, order a drink, order food, ask for the bill, pay, say goodbye. Use «quisiera» once, «por favor» twice, and no English. Then change the order to two people — «¿algo para picar?» — which forces the plural forms and is where learners slip from tú to vosotros (or ustedes, on the American side).
